exercises.name: Chin tuck
exercises.cue: Slide your chin straight back (make a soft double chin). Keep eyes level — don’t tip the nose down.
exercises.commonMistake: Tipping the head up or down instead of sliding straight back.
exercises.cuePrevious: Slide your chin straight back — soft double-chin, eyes still on the screen.

seated.cue: Slide your chin straight back (make a soft double chin). Keep eyes level — don’t tip the nose down. Stay seated tall.

standing.cue: Stand tall. Slide your chin straight back (soft double chin). Eyes level — don’t tip the nose down.
standing.selectionRule: If program.setup===standing and file exists, use {id}-standing.svg; else fallback to {id}.svg

exercises.name: Neck side stretch
exercises.cue: Sit or stand tall. Tip one ear toward the same-side shoulder; rest the opposite hand lightly on the head. Don’t pull hard.
exercises.commonMistake: Yanking or twisting the neck.
exercises.cuePrevious: Ear toward shoulder; opposite hand rests lightly on the head.

exercises.name: Neck rotation
exercises.cue: Turn your head slowly to look over one shoulder, pause, return to center, then the other side.
exercises.commonMistake: Forcing past a comfortable range.
exercises.cuePrevious: Slowly turn left, pause, then right.

exercises.name: Upper trap release
exercises.cue: Sit tall. Drop one ear toward that shoulder and look slightly down toward the armpit. Keep the opposite shoulder down.
exercises.commonMistake: Shrugging the stretching shoulder up.
exercises.cuePrevious: Sit tall, drop one ear toward the shoulder, look slightly down.

exercises.name: Seated scap squeeze
exercises.cue: Sitting tall, draw your shoulder blades together and slightly down. Hold briefly, then release. Don’t shrug up toward your ears.
exercises.commonMistake: Shrugging shoulders up toward the ears.
exercises.cuePrevious: Pinch your shoulder blades into your back pockets — down, not up into your ears.

exercises.name: Thoracic extension over chair
exercises.cue: Sit with mid-back against the chair back, hands lightly behind your head. Lean the upper back over the chair while keeping the low back quiet.
exercises.commonMistake: Hyperextending the low back.
exercises.cuePrevious: Hands behind head; gently lean upper back over the chair back.

exercises.name: Seated cat-cow
exercises.cue: Sitting, round your mid-back and tuck the chin slightly (cat), then lift the chest and look forward (cow). Move slow.
exercises.commonMistake: Rushing or forcing end range.
exercises.cuePrevious: Round the spine, then open the chest — slow and smooth.

exercises.name: Doorway or wall chest opener
exercises.cue: Place a forearm on a doorframe or wall at about shoulder height. Gently turn your chest away until you feel a stretch across the front of the shoulder and chest.
exercises.commonMistake: Leaning so hard the front of the shoulder hurts.
exercises.cuePrevious: Forearm on frame or wall; gently turn the body away.

exercises.name: Shoulder rolls
exercises.cue: Slow shoulder circles — lift, roll back, drop, then forward. Keep the neck easy.
exercises.commonMistake: Rushing or crunching the neck.
exercises.cuePrevious: Slow shoulder circles: sweep back like you’re peeling sticky notes off your upper back.

seated.cue: Slow shoulder circles — lift, roll back, drop, then forward. Keep the neck easy. Sit tall, arms relaxed.

standing.cue: Slow shoulder circles — lift, roll back, drop, then forward. Keep the neck easy. Soft knees, ribs quiet.
standing.selectionRule: If program.setup===standing and file exists, use {id}-standing.svg; else fallback to {id}.svg

exercises.name: Wall angels
exercises.cue: Stand (or sit tall) with back against a wall or firm chair back. Keep ribs quiet and slide both arms up and down the surface like a slow snow angel, trying to keep contact.
exercises.commonMistake: Arching the low back off the wall.
exercises.cuePrevious: Back to wall or chair; slide arms up like a slow snow angel.

exercises.name: Wrist flexor stretch
exercises.cue: Arm forward, elbow soft, palm facing up. Use the other hand to gently ease the fingers toward the floor until you feel a stretch in the forearm.
exercises.commonMistake: Locking the elbow hard.
exercises.cuePrevious: Arm out, palm up; ease fingers toward the floor until the forearm wakes up.

exercises.name: Wrist extensor stretch
exercises.cue: Arm forward, elbow soft, palm facing down. Use the other hand to gently ease the fingers toward you until you feel a stretch on top of the forearm.
exercises.commonMistake: Bouncing into the stretch.
exercises.cuePrevious: Arm out, palm down; gently pull fingers toward you.

exercises.name: Wrist circles
exercises.cue: Make a loose fist or open hand and circle the wrist slowly one way, then the other.
exercises.commonMistake: Forcing through sharp pain.
exercises.cuePrevious: Slow circles in both directions.

exercises.name: Finger fans
exercises.cue: Spread all fingers wide, then close into a soft fist. Repeat without clenching hard.
exercises.commonMistake: Clenching hard if hands are sore.
exercises.cuePrevious: Spread fingers wide, then make a soft fist.

exercises.name: Seated figure-4
exercises.cue: Sit tall. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Hinge a little forward from the hips until you feel a stretch in the outer hip — stop before sharp pain.
exercises.commonMistake: Pressing down on the bent knee.
exercises.cuePrevious: Ankle on opposite knee; tip forward an inch until the hip says ah — not ouch.

exercises.name: Seated hip opener
exercises.cue: Sit tall with feet planted. Slowly open both knees outward, then bring them back toward center.
exercises.commonMistake: Collapsing the low back.
exercises.cuePrevious: Sit tall; open knees outward with feet planted.

exercises.name: Standing hip flexor stretch
exercises.cue: Stand and step one foot back into a short lunge. Gently tuck the back-side pelvis under (flatten the low-back arch) until you feel a stretch in the front of the back hip. Hold the desk for balance if needed.
exercises.commonMistake: Arching the low back.
exercises.notes: Hold desk for balance if needed.
exercises.accessNote: Free for Standing Desk Reset; still listed in full library.
exercises.cuePrevious: Step one foot back; gently tuck the pelvis.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.cue: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Squeeze the glutes and lift the hips until shoulders–hips–knees line up. Lower slow. Stop if the low back hurts.
exercises.commonMistake: Pushing through low-back pain.
exercises.cuePrevious: Lie down, squeeze glutes, lift hips.

exercises.name: Standing glute squeeze
exercises.cue: Stand with soft knees. Squeeze the glutes firmly for a few seconds, then release. Don’t lock the knees.
exercises.commonMistake: Locking the knees.
exercises.accessNote: Free for Standing Desk Reset; still listed in full library.
exercises.cuePrevious: Soft knees; squeeze glutes for 3 seconds.

exercises.name: Calf raise
exercises.cue: Stand holding the desk if needed. Rise onto the balls of both feet, pause, then lower slowly.
exercises.commonMistake: Bouncing at the top.
exercises.notes: Hold desk for balance if needed.
exercises.accessNote: Free for Standing Desk Reset; still listed in full library.
exercises.cuePrevious: Rise onto toes, then lower slowly.

exercises.name: Ankle circles
exercises.cue: Lift one foot slightly and circle the ankle slowly each direction. Switch feet.
exercises.commonMistake: Rushing the circles.
exercises.cuePrevious: Lift one foot; circle slowly both ways.

exercises.name: Seated march
exercises.cue: Sit tall and lift one knee, then the other, like a slow march in the chair.
exercises.commonMistake: Leaning hard on the chair arms.
exercises.cuePrevious: Lift knees alternately while seated.

exercises.name: Standing quad stretch
exercises.cue: Stand holding the desk. Bend one knee and hold that ankle behind you, keeping the knees close together. Don’t twist the knee out.
exercises.commonMistake: Twisting the knee outward.
exercises.cuePrevious: Hold ankle behind you; keep knees close; hold the desk.

exercises.name: Hamstring hinge (desk-assisted)
exercises.cue: Stand with soft knees, hands light on the desk. Hinge forward from the hips with a long spine — don’t round hard through the low back.
exercises.commonMistake: Rounding hard through the low back.
exercises.cuePrevious: Soft knees; hinge at hips with hands on the desk.

exercises.name: Seated pelvic tilts
exercises.cue: Sit tall. Gently rock the pelvis to flatten the low back against the chair, then tip the other way to recreate a small low-back curve.
exercises.commonMistake: Forcing a big range of motion.
exercises.cuePrevious: Gently rock pelvis to flatten then arch the low back.

exercises.name: Seated side bend
exercises.cue: Sit tall. Reach one arm overhead and lean gently to the opposite side, lengthening the side body. Don’t collapse forward.
exercises.commonMistake: Collapsing forward instead of lengthening.
exercises.cuePrevious: Reach one arm overhead and lean gently to the side.

exercises.name: Desk plank lean
exercises.cue: Hands on the desk, walk the feet back until the body is in a straight line from head to heels. Hold without sagging the hips or shrugging. Use forearms on the desk if wrists complain.
exercises.commonMistake: Sagging hips or shrugging shoulders.
exercises.notes: Use forearms on desk if wrists complain.
exercises.cuePrevious: Hands on desk, body in a straight line; hold.

exercises.name: Standing posture reset
exercises.cue: Stand with feet under the hips, soft knees. Stack ears over shoulders over hips. Grow tall through the crown of the head without locking the knees or flaring the ribs.
exercises.commonMistake: Locking knees or puffing the chest.
exercises.cuePrevious: Feet under hips, soft knees, tall through the crown of the head.

exercises.name: Box breathing
exercises.cue: Breathe in for 4 counts, hold 4, out for 4, hold 4. Repeat for the cued rounds. Keep it easy — don’t strain.
exercises.commonMistake: Straining or forcing the breath.
exercises.cuePrevious: In 4, hold 4, out 4, hold 4.

exercises.name: Long exhale reset
exercises.cue: Inhale through the nose, then sigh out through the mouth for longer than the inhale. Soft shoulders. Stop if you feel lightheaded.
exercises.commonMistake: Breathing too fast (hyperventilating).
exercises.cuePrevious: Nose in, longer mouth sigh out — like fogging a quiet window.

seated.cue: Inhale through the nose, then sigh out through the mouth for longer than the inhale. Soft shoulders. Stop if you feel lightheaded. Sit soft and tall.

standing.cue: Stand with soft knees. Inhale through the nose, then sigh out through the mouth longer than the inhale. Soft shoulders.
standing.selectionRule: If program.setup===standing and file exists, use {id}-standing.svg; else fallback to {id}.svg

exercises.name: Sit bones find
exercises.cue: Sit and rock gently side to side and front to back until you feel both sit bones on the chair, then sit tall balanced on them.
exercises.commonMistake: Perching on the tailbone or slumping off the sit bones.
exercises.cuePrevious: Rock gently on the chair until you feel both sit bones, then sit tall on them.

exercises.name: Suboccipital nod
exercises.cue: Fingertips at the base of the skull. Make a tiny yes-nod (chin slightly in) and release. Soft and slow — not a big chin-to-chest tuck.
exercises.commonMistake: Big chin-to-chest nods or pressing hard with the hands.
exercises.cuePrevious: Fingertips at the base of the skull; make a tiny yes-nod, soft and slow.

exercises.name: Chin tuck hold
exercises.cue: Slide the chin straight back into a soft double chin and hold. Eyes level. Then release.
exercises.commonMistake: Nodding the nose down instead of gliding straight back.
exercises.cuePrevious: Slide chin straight back into a gentle double chin and hold.

exercises.name: Chair open chest
exercises.cue: Sit tall, hands lightly behind the head, elbows wide. Lift the breastbone a little without jamming the low back or flaring the ribs.
exercises.commonMistake: Flaring the ribs and overarching the low back.
exercises.cuePrevious: Hands behind head, elbows wide; tiny lift through the breastbone without jamming the low back.

exercises.name: Unshrug
exercises.cue: Let the shoulders slide down away from the ears. Lightly draw the shoulder blades down the back. Don’t force the chest forward.
exercises.commonMistake: Pinching the neck or forcing the chest forward.
exercises.cuePrevious: Drop your shoulders away from your earrings — blades melt into back pockets.

exercises.name: Short foot grip
exercises.cue: With feet on the floor, gently shorten the midfoot as if gripping the floor — keep the toes soft, not clawed.
exercises.commonMistake: Clawing hard with the toes or holding the breath.
exercises.notes: Works seated or standing at the desk.
exercises.cuePrevious: Gently grip the floor with the midfoot; keep toes soft.

exercises.name: Standing hip hinge (desk)
exercises.cue: Stand with soft knees, hands light on the desk. Push the hips back and hinge forward with a long spine, then return tall.
exercises.commonMistake: Rounding the low back instead of hinging at the hips.
exercises.cuePrevious: Soft knees; hinge at the hips with hands light on the desk; spine long.

exercises.name: Scap pack hold
exercises.cue: Draw the shoulder blades slightly together and down, as if packing them into the back pockets. Hold without shrugging. Release.
exercises.commonMistake: Shrugging up or over-pinching the shoulder blades.
exercises.cuePrevious: Draw shoulder blades slightly together and down; hold without shrugging.

exercises.name: Seated lumbar support reset
exercises.cue: Sit on your sit bones. Allow a gentle natural curve in the low back (a small towel roll behind the low back is optional). Don’t force a big arch or thrust the ribs out.
exercises.commonMistake: Forcing a big arch or thrusting the ribs out.
exercises.cuePrevious: Sit tall on sit bones; allow a gentle natural low-back curve (towel roll optional).

exercises.name: Walk-to-water march
exercises.cue: March in place easily or take a short walk (for example to get water). Quiet feet, easy breathing — not a workout.
exercises.commonMistake: Turning it into a workout or stomping.
exercises.cuePrevious: Easy march in place or a short walk to get water — keep it quiet and easy.

exercises.name: Elbows-pinned external rotation + scap squeeze
exercises.cue: Elbows stay glued to your sides. Rotate the palms outward (external rotation), then lightly squeeze the shoulder blades down and together. Return and repeat.
exercises.commonMistake: Letting elbows flare or shrugging toward the ears.
exercises.notes: Desk-adapted ER + scap pack. Inspired by desk/posture catalogs; original DeskBreak cueing.
exercises.cuePrevious: Elbows glued to your sides; rotate palms out, then lightly squeeze shoulder blades down and together.

exercises.name: Seated thoracic rotation
exercises.cue: Sit tall with feet planted. Rotate the mid-back to look over one shoulder, then the other. Keep the hips quiet — don’t twist from the low back.
exercises.commonMistake: Twisting from the low back or yanking with the arms.
exercises.cuePrevious: Sit tall; rotate mid-back left and right with hips quiet and breath easy.

exercises.name: Standing overhead reach
exercises.cue: Stand tall with soft knees. Reach both arms overhead slowly, lengthening through the sides. Keep ribs soft (don’t flare) and breathe easy.
exercises.commonMistake: Flared ribs, shrugged shoulders, or locking the knees.
exercises.cuePrevious: Stand tall; reach both arms up slow, lengthen the sides, soft ribs, easy breath.

exercises.name: Seated hip windshield wipers
exercises.cue: Sit tall, feet planted. Slowly sweep both knees to one side, then the other, like windshield wipers — moving at the hips, not collapsing the low back.
exercises.commonMistake: Collapsing the low back or forcing end range.
exercises.notes: More specific than seated-hip-opener; keep both.
exercises.cuePrevious: Feet planted; slowly sweep knees left and right like windshield wipers (hip IR/ER).

exercises.name: Sit-to-stand + glute squeeze
exercises.cue: From sitting, stand up (use hands on thighs/desk only if needed). Squeeze the glutes at the top, then sit down slowly with control.
exercises.commonMistake: Knee cave, rushing, or pushing off with momentum only.
exercises.notes: Hold desk for balance if needed.
exercises.cuePrevious: Stand up from the chair without using hands if you can; squeeze glutes at the top, then sit slow.

exercises.name: Foot tripod + toe spread
exercises.cue: Feel three points on the floor: big-toe base, little-toe base, and heel. Spread the toes wide, then keep a soft grip through the midfoot.
exercises.commonMistake: Clawing toes hard or rolling to the outer edge only.
exercises.notes: Pairs with short-foot-grip; feet→hips chain start. No -b by design (close-up; L/R N/A).
exercises.cuePrevious: Feel big toe, little toe, and heel on the floor; spread toes wide, then soft grip.

exercises.name: Desk wiggle reset
exercises.cue: Stay seated. For about 30 seconds, make small easy movements through the hips, ribs, and shoulders — a quiet wiggle, not big swings.
exercises.commonMistake: Going big/loud in an open office — keep it micro.
exercises.notes: Delight/micro-move for free library. Quiet enough for open office.
exercises.cuePrevious: Thirty seconds of tiny chair dances — hips, ribs, shoulders — like shaking crumbs off a sweater.

exercises.name: Screen distance + blink
exercises.cue: Sit or stand slightly farther from the screen. Soften your gaze to a far point (wall or window), take five slow blinks, then return to work.
exercises.commonMistake: Staring hard or skipping the far-focus.
exercises.notes: Free delight; pairs with chin tuck / posture. Not a medical eye exercise — just a screen break habit.
exercises.cuePrevious: Push back an inch, soften your gaze to the far wall, slow blink ×5, then return.

exercises.name: Standing wrist shake-out
exercises.cue: Stand with arms relaxed. Gently shake out the hands, then circle the wrists a few times each direction. Keep shoulders down.
exercises.commonMistake: Tensing the shoulders up by the ears while shaking.
exercises.notes: Standing-native wrist relief for Standing Desk Reset (not a seated stretch swap).
exercises.cuePrevious: Arms relaxed at your sides; gently shake out the hands and roll the wrists for a few seconds each way.

programs.name: 2-min Desk Reset

steps.positionCue: Slide your chin straight back (make a soft double chin). Keep eyes level — don’t tip the nose down. Stay seated tall.
Slow shoulder circles — lift, roll back, drop, then forward. Keep the neck easy. Sit tall, arms relaxed.
Inhale through the nose, then sigh out through the mouth for longer than the inhale. Soft shoulders. Stop if you feel lightheaded. Sit soft and tall.

programs.tagline: Prefer to stay seated? Same two minutes, chair edition.
programs.startPrompt: No need to stand — this one’s built for the chair.
programs.benefitHeadline: Interrupt the sit before it stacks up
programs.benefitUi: 2 minutes of light movement can ease stiffness, nudge alertness, and break up long sits — without leaving your desk zone.

benefitBlurbs.title: Ease desk stiffness
benefitBlurbs.body: Short active microbreaks (about 2–3 minutes of light movement) are linked with less perceived musculoskeletal discomfort versus staying locked in one posture.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Changing joint angles and lightly loading muscles reduces continuous tissue strain from static sitting.

benefitBlurbs.title: Protect alertness
benefitBlurbs.body: Breaking long sits with brief light activity helps counter the dip in how awake and sharp people feel during unbroken desk work.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Posture change + light muscle work; related research on walking breaks shows they can help maintain cerebral blood flow that otherwise drifts down with prolonged sitting.

benefitBlurbs.title: Feasible every meeting gap
benefitBlurbs.body: Tiny resets are easier to repeat than a workout — and frequency of sit-breaks matters as much as total exercise minutes for many desk-day effects.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Habit stacking: short bouts accumulate across the day without needing a gym or outfit change.

programs.benefitDetail: Research on active microbreaks suggests ~2–3 minutes of light movement can ease desk discomfort and help you stay sharper than sitting locked in one pose. Tiny resets also stack — how often you break up sitting matters, not just gym minutes.
programs.doneLine: Two minutes well spent. Your joints just got a meeting break.

programs.name: 5-min Lunch Reset
programs.goal: Hips + chest open, energy up, office-appropriate.
programs.tagline: Midday unkink — no gym bag, no weird looks.
programs.benefitUi: Five minutes to open hips and chest, wake your back, and push blood through legs after a sit block — a true midday reset.

benefitBlurbs.title: Undo the laptop shape
benefitBlurbs.body: Five minutes is enough to open hips and chest, wake scapular muscles, and reset head-over-ribs alignment after a morning of screen work.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Targets common desk adaptations: hip-flexor shortening, thoracic rounding, and forward-head posture.

benefitBlurbs.title: Cut the afternoon slump signal
benefitBlurbs.body: Active breaks are associated with lower perceived fatigue and job stress versus unbroken sedentary stretches.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Light whole-body movement + breathing arousal the nervous system without needing a hard workout.

benefitBlurbs.title: Move blood, not just stretch
benefitBlurbs.body: Standing + calf/hip work helps circulation in the legs after hours of chair compression.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Muscle pump in the lower body supports venous return; frequent contractile activity is also studied for metabolic markers in office workers.

programs.cardLine: Open hips and chest; wake energy mid-day.
programs.benefitDetail: Five minutes is enough to undo the laptop shape — hips, chest, upper back — and light standing work helps circulation after a sit block. Active breaks are also linked with less perceived fatigue than unbroken desk time.
programs.doneLine: Midday unkink complete. Blood moved. Brain slightly less mush.

programs.name: 10-min Busy-Day Circuit
programs.seoHook: home workout routine for busy days
programs.goal: Full-body undo after a heavy sit day.
programs.tagline: Sit-day cleanup. Ten minutes, full stack.
programs.benefitUi: Ten minutes to unkink the full desk chain — neck to calves — and interrupt a long sit with a real movement bout.

benefitBlurbs.title: Broader relief coverage
benefitBlurbs.body: A longer circuit hits neck, mid-back, wrists, hips, and legs in one pass — useful after a heavy sit day when one area isn’t the only complaint.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Addresses multiple tissue regions that stiffen under sustained flexion and static load.

benefitBlurbs.title: Stronger sit-interrupt dose
benefitBlurbs.body: Ten minutes of continuous light movement is a meaningful sedentary interruption — closer to a short activity bout than a stretch snack.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Accumulated light activity improves the pattern of sitting interruption; cardiometabolic studies emphasize break pattern, not only total gym minutes.

benefitBlurbs.title: End-of-day downshift
benefitBlurbs.body: Pair mobility with slower breathing so the session finishes calm, not amped — better for leaving work mode.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Longer exhales support a parasympathetic shift after a stimulatory movement block.

programs.cardLine: Full desk-chain reset after a heavy sit day.
programs.benefitDetail: A longer circuit hits neck to calves in one pass — a real sit-interrupt, not just a stretch snack. Breaking up long sitting with light movement is studied for comfort and for how the body handles a sedentary day; breathe out slow at the end to leave work mode calmer.
programs.doneLine: Full-stack cleanup done. The chair can have you back — briefly.

evidenceNotes: Active microbreaks systematic review (office workers): short light-intensity breaks (~2–3 min) associated with physical/mental benefits without clear productivity harm (Cogent Engineering, 2022).
Walking breaks & cerebral blood flow: regular short walking breaks can prevent the CBF decline seen with prolonged sitting (J Appl Physiol, 2018).
Sedentary-break frequency meta-analysis: interrupting sitting more often (e.g. ~every 30 min) tends to favor glucose responses vs rarer breaks (randomized crossover evidence).
2min.uiShort: 2 minutes of light movement can ease stiffness, nudge alertness, and break up long sits — without leaving your desk zone.

5min.headline: A real posture + energy reset

blurbs.title: Undo the laptop shape
blurbs.body: Five minutes is enough to open hips and chest, wake scapular muscles, and reset head-over-ribs alignment after a morning of screen work.
blurbs.mechanism: Targets common desk adaptations: hip-flexor shortening, thoracic rounding, and forward-head posture.

blurbs.title: Cut the afternoon slump signal
blurbs.body: Active breaks are associated with lower perceived fatigue and job stress versus unbroken sedentary stretches.
blurbs.mechanism: Light whole-body movement + breathing arousal the nervous system without needing a hard workout.

blurbs.title: Move blood, not just stretch
blurbs.body: Standing + calf/hip work helps circulation in the legs after hours of chair compression.
blurbs.mechanism: Muscle pump in the lower body supports venous return; frequent contractile activity is also studied for metabolic markers in office workers.

evidenceNotes: Movement microbreaks & mood/stress: pilot RCT evidence that movement microbreaks during work can relate to later reductions in job-related stress (Frontiers in Public Health, 2020).
Hourly micro-exercise (~3 min) trials in office workers explore metabolic markers (glucose/insulin) with equipment-free workplace moves (BMC Public Health, 2026).
Workplace physiotherapy / micro-break literature: stretching and postural re-education are commonly used for MSD risk management (mixed but supportive evidence quality).
5min.uiShort: Five minutes to open hips and chest, wake your back, and push blood through legs after a sit block — a true midday reset.

10min.headline: Full-stack sit-day cleanup

blurbs.title: Broader relief coverage
blurbs.body: A longer circuit hits neck, mid-back, wrists, hips, and legs in one pass — useful after a heavy sit day when one area isn’t the only complaint.
blurbs.mechanism: Addresses multiple tissue regions that stiffen under sustained flexion and static load.

blurbs.title: Stronger sit-interrupt dose
blurbs.body: Ten minutes of continuous light movement is a meaningful sedentary interruption — closer to a short activity bout than a stretch snack.
blurbs.mechanism: Accumulated light activity improves the pattern of sitting interruption; cardiometabolic studies emphasize break pattern, not only total gym minutes.

blurbs.title: End-of-day downshift
blurbs.body: Pair mobility with slower breathing so the session finishes calm, not amped — better for leaving work mode.
blurbs.mechanism: Longer exhales support a parasympathetic shift after a stimulatory movement block.

evidenceNotes: Same microbreak / sedentary-interruption literature as above, scaled to a longer single bout.
Waongenngarm et al. and related break reviews: active breaks with postural change/stretching often help discomfort vs continuous sitting (evidence quality varies by outcome).
Does not replace medical care for injury, or replace moderate–vigorous exercise guidelines for long-term health.
10min.uiShort: Ten minutes to unkink the full desk chain — neck to calves — and interrupt a long sit with a real movement bout.

standingVsSeated.whySeparate: Standing resets emphasize hip extension, calf muscle pump, and upright stack. Seated resets emphasize neck/wrist access and hip external rotation without leaving the chair. Same goal, different mechanics — not a posture swap of the same steps.

2.cardLine: Short moves ease stiffness and nudge alertness.
2.detail: Research on active microbreaks suggests ~2–3 minutes of light movement can ease desk discomfort and help you stay sharper than sitting locked in one pose. Tiny resets also stack — how often you break up sitting matters, not just gym minutes.
2.doneLine: Two minutes well spent. Your joints just got a meeting break.

5.cardLine: Open hips and chest; wake energy mid-day.
5.detail: Five minutes is enough to undo the laptop shape — hips, chest, upper back — and light standing work helps circulation after a sit block. Active breaks are also linked with less perceived fatigue than unbroken desk time.
5.doneLine: Midday unkink complete. Blood moved. Brain slightly less mush.

10.cardLine: Full desk-chain reset after a heavy sit day.
10.detail: A longer circuit hits neck to calves in one pass — a real sit-interrupt, not just a stretch snack. Breaking up long sitting with light movement is studied for comfort and for how the body handles a sedentary day; breathe out slow at the end to leave work mode calmer.
10.doneLine: Full-stack cleanup done. The chair can have you back — briefly.

onboardingBenefits.beat: Quick resets beat heroic workouts you’ll skip.

cueAudit.summary: Full cue accuracy pass. Removed confusing metaphors (e.g. sticky-notes shoulder rolls). Shared moves gained setupVariants for seated vs standing assets/cues.
cueAudit.shoulderRollsWas: Slow shoulder circles: sweep back like you’re peeling sticky notes off your upper back.
cueAudit.shoulderRollsNow: Slow shoulder circles: lift the shoulders up, roll them back, drop them down, then bring them forward. Reverse direction when cued.
